subject.title: fix(plugin-sdk): update ssrf-runtime import path in cdp-proxy-bypass

question: Should `fetchConfiguredLocalOriginWithSsrFGuard` and `registerManagedProxyBrowserCdpBypass` become public `openclaw/plugin-sdk/ssrf-runtime` exports, or should the package fix preserve owner-scoped private Browser/Ollama access?
rationale: Current source and scoped policy intentionally keep these managed-proxy/SSRF helpers private to bundled Browser/Ollama owners, so automation cannot choose the permanent SDK/security boundary.

options.title: Keep Owner-Scoped Private Access
options.body: Repair the packaged Browser/Ollama load path through the existing private bundled-plugin alias or another narrow private seam without publishing these helpers to all SDK consumers.

options.title: Promote As Public SDK Contract
options.body: Land the public `ssrf-runtime` promotion only with maintainer approval, docs/export/baseline guardrails, and packaged Browser/Ollama proof.

options.title: Pause For Canonical Direction
options.body: Hold this branch until maintainers choose between this public-barrel approach and the sibling private-subpath compatibility approaches for the canonical regression.

recommendation.title: Keep Owner-Scoped Private Access
recommendation.body: Repair the packaged Browser/Ollama load path through the existing private bundled-plugin alias or another narrow private seam without publishing these helpers to all SDK consumers.

likelyOwner.reason: The PR is currently assigned to `steipete`, and the package-boundary history makes him the clearest available owner for the SDK/security boundary choice.
